text: When an ECP5 FIR is DSP-capped at 12>8 while timing has margin (235.7 MHz, 4.24 ns carry-chain accumulator), do not apply symmetric fold=2 with dsp_regs=in_pipe_out without checking the pre-multiplier path: it reaches 8 DSP but Fmax falls to 100.7 MHz because the 2:1 operand mux/coefficient ROM makes FF part[1] -> LUT4 out_data -> carry-chain the 9.93 ns critical path.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR meets its 8-DSP cap at fold=2 but is timing-limited by the post-multiplier gather into a 36-cell carry chain over 4.33 ns of route, insert two fabric pipeline stages after the multiplier (pipe_mul 0→2) to split the accumulation path, gaining +11.2 MHz (100.7→111.9 MHz) for +2 LUT and 0 DSP.

When an ECP5 symmetric-folded FIR with 8 DSPs is timing-limited at 111.9 MHz by a fabric path of part[0] FF → 6-LUT4 out_data tree → 34-cell carry chain, avoid changing acc_width 40→38, pipe_mul 2→3, and reg_in false→true: it cut LUTs by 43 but dropped Fmax 6.4 MHz to 105.5 MHz with no DSP savings and remained infeasible because the accumulator/fabric sum, not the multiplier pipeline, dominates.

When a symmetric folded FIR on ECP5 is timing-limited by routing through the tap-operand mux/coefficient ROM (critical path FF -> 5-cell LUT4 (~4.2 ns route) -> 33-cell carry chain, no DSP), increase fold from 2 to 4 (halving DSPs from 8 to 4) to relieve pre-multiplier congestion, which shortens the carry chain to 9 cells and raises Fmax by 24.3 MHz (105.5 to 129.8 MHz) while cutting 457 LUTs.

When the ECP5 4-fold symmetric FIR hits 129.8 MHz on the 17-bit pre-adder carry chain (2.29 ns) into the MULT18X18D A input, de-share the coefficients and double fold to 8 to keep 4 MACs/4 DSPs and cut the pre-adder, but the replacement 3-level 8:1 operand mux becomes critical, so LUTs fall 137 while Fmax drops 3.5 MHz to 126.3 MHz—fix the mux or leave the pre-adder.

On ECP5 FIRs, when DSP-count-bound at 12 MULT18X18D against a 6-DSP cap while timing has margin at 4.29 ns/233 MHz, switch to symmetric fold=4 with reg_in=true and dsp_regs=in_pipe_out, and set acc_width=38, to reach 4 DSP/963 LUT/131 MHz feasible at 1/4 sample-per-cycle because the critical path moves to the pre-adder carry chain into the MULT18X18D A input and the minimum 38-bit accumulator shortens the post-multiplier carry chain.

On ECP5 folded symmetric FIR, do not halve fold from 4 to 2 while changing dsp_regs from in_pipe_out to none and pipe_mul from 0 to 2 to double throughput: it doubles DSPs 4→8 and LUTs 963→1417, and the critical path grows from 7.63 ns (x_d[0]→pre-adder carry→mux) to 12.84 ns (x_d[0]→13-cell g_mac[1].u_m.m carry chain), so Fmax falls 131.0→77.9 MHz and the design loses feasibility.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is timing-limited at 77.9 MHz with 8 DSPs, keep the 2-stage multiplier pipeline rather than dropping it to 0, because that removal cut Fmax to 61.2 MHz (-16.6 MHz) with no LUT/DSP change as the critical path shifted into the carry-chain MAC accumulation (12.84->16.33 ns).

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is DSP/timing-limited at 61.2 MHz with 8 DSPs, don't raise the fold from 2 to 4 to meet a 6-DSP limit because although it cuts DSPs to 4 and LUTs by 455, it deepens the MAC carry chain from 5 to 15 cells and lowers Fmax to 57.6 MHz.

When an ECP5 FIR has 12 MULT18X18D exceeding the 6-DSP cap but timing has margin (233 MHz with a 4.29 ns carry-chain accumulator), switch to symmetric fold=4 with reg_in=true, dsp_regs=in_pipe_out, and acc_width=38 to reach 4 DSP and feasibility, accepting fmax down to 131 MHz as the critical path moves to the 3-cell pre-adder carry chain feeding the DSP A input.

When an ECP5 FIR is resource-blocked by 12 DSPs against a 6-DSP cap while timing is comfortable, switch to symmetric fold=4 with reg_in=true, dsp_regs=in_pipe_out, and acc_width=38 to cut to 4 DSP and 963 LUT and become feasible, accepting the Fmax drop to 131 MHz because the critical path shifts from the 35-cell accumulator carry chain to the folded multiplier/accumulator carry chain.

When an ECP5 FIR misses only on DSP count (12 MULT18X18D vs a 6-DSP cap) while its 233 MHz path is a 35-cell accumulator carry chain, go symmetric fold=4 with reg_in=true, in_pipe_out DSP registers, and a 38-bit accumulator to hit 4 DSP / 963 LUT / 131 MHz at 1/4 throughput, because 4:1 folding cuts unique MACs to 16 and relocates the critical path to the DSP pre-adder/A-input carry chain.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR using 4 DSPs at 0.25 samples/cycle is already feasible with ~21 MHz slack and its critical path is input FF -> pre-adder carry chain -> MULT18X18D, drop the input register to save 1 LUT (963->962) and a fabric FF; Fmax holds at ~131.4 MHz (+0.4 MHz) because the slack absorbs the longer input-to-pre-adder route while the bottleneck remains the multiplier operand-mux/pre-adder cone.

When an ECP5 FIR fails only on DSP count (12 MULT18X18D > 6) while timing has margin (233 MHz, 35-cell accumulator carry chain, 4.29 ns), switch to symmetric fold=4 with explicit in_pipe_out DSPs and a 38-bit accumulator, which drops to 4 DSPs and 963 LUT and is feasible at 131 MHz because the critical path moves to the pre-adder carry chain feeding the DSP A input.

When an ECP5 transposed FIR exceeds the 6-DSP cap with 12 inferred MULT18X18D but has a comfortable 233 MHz frequency, increase symmetric fold from 1 to 4, set acc_width=38, and enable reg_in and in_pipe_out DSP registers to cut DSP to 4 and LUT to 963, accepting a drop to 131 MHz because the critical path moves from the 35-cell post-accumulator carry chain to the shorter DSP pre-adder/A-input carry chain.

On an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR that is feasible with ~21 MHz slack and only LUT reduction matters, drop the redundant input register: it saves 1 LUT (963→962) with DSP count unchanged at 4 and raises Fmax 131.0→131.4 MHz because the added input-to-pre-adder route is absorbed by slack while the critical path remains the pre-adder/MULT18X18D A-input cone.

When an ECP5 folded FIR is capped at 4 DSPs and the behavioral-multiplier run dies in simulation with no critical path, instantiate 4 explicit MULT18X18D at symmetric fold=2 (0.5 samples/cycle) and enable reg_in, pipe_in, in_pipe_out, pipe_mul, and sum_tree to remove the x_d→pre-adder/tap-mux→DSP-A path and split the 4-term partial-sum carry chain, making the design timing-feasible at 209.6 MHz with 459 LUTs.

On an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR pinned at the 4-DSP cap and timing-limited by the pre-adder carry chain into pipe_in, drop the redundant input register and cut acc_width from 32 to 29 bits to remove the head FF/route and shrink the M=4 reducer, gaining 8.1 MHz (209.6→217.7 MHz) and 15 LUTs with no DSP change.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is pinned at the DSP cap and its critical path is a 26-cell accumulator carry chain (4.59 ns, Fmax 217.7 MHz), enabling the input register (reg_in) retimes the MAC operand path, shrinks the limiting carry chain to 23 cells (4.48 ns), and raises Fmax to 223.1 MHz (+5.3 MHz) for +1 LUT and no extra DSP, so use it as a cheap first knob before narrowing accumulator width.

On the ECP5 folded symmetric FIR at the 4-DSP cap whose critical path is input FF -> pre-adder carry chain -> MULT operand, keep acc_width at 29 with reg_in=true rather than widening to 32 and dropping the head register, which added 13 LUTs and cost 9.1 MHz (223.1 -> 213.9 MHz) by lengthening the accumulator carry chain.

On an ECP5 FIR, when acc_in_dsp=true is Xilinx-only and sim/timing fails, switch to symmetric fold=2 with acc_in_dsp=false, dsp_regs=in_pipe_out, pipe_mul=2, reg_in/pipe_in/sum_tree enabled to hit the 4-DSP cap at 0.5 samples/cycle and 219.3 MHz, since the 4.56 ns critical path then becomes the a_ext carry chain (1.17 ns logic + 1.43 ns route) rather than an illegal DSP accumulator.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR with 4 DSPs at fold=2 is carry-chain-limited at 219 MHz, do not drop the registered sum tree for a third multiplier pipeline stage: it moves the critical path to the 23-cell out_data carry chain and cuts Fmax to 156 MHz (-63.3 MHz) for +70 LUTs.

When an ECP5 symmetric folded FIR is timing-limited by a 23-cell out_data carry chain at 156.0 MHz with 4 DSPs, go to fold=4 with sum-tree on and 2-stage multiplier pipe to halve DSPs to 2 and shorten the MAC carry chain to 12 cells, raising fmax to 195.4 MHz (+39.4 MHz) at 0.25 samples/cycle and -109 LUTs.

When an ECP5 symmetric FIR at fold=4 with DSP input/output registers is feasible at 195.4 MHz and limited by the FF→pre-adder carry-chain→LUT path, do not halve the fold to 2 and remove DSP pipelining—it doubles DSPs from 2 to 4, puts the 3.93 ns MULT18X18D plus long routing on the critical path, and drops Fmax to 119.4 MHz, losing feasibility.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is timing-limited at 119.4 MHz by the 8.38 ns FF→MULT18X18D→FF cone, deepen the multiplier pipeline from 2 to 3 stages and enable DSP input/pipeline/output registers (`none`→`in_pipe_out`), which cuts the multiplier path out of the critical cone and leaves a 4.56 ns accumulator carry chain, yielding 219.3 MHz (+99.9 MHz) with LUT/DSP unchanged.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR is already feasible at 219.3 MHz but timing-limited by the DSP-register-to-accumulator carry chain (4.56 ns, 1.67 ns carry logic + 1.39 ns route), removing the input register and reducing pipe_mul 3 to 2 shortens the path to the acc[0] carry chain (4.50 ns, 1.60 ns logic) for +2.8 MHz at -1 LUT and unchanged DSPs.
